Where things stand

Your work has moved on. Your website hasn't yet.

Mahé Design & Build has been building across Seychelles since 2002, with a Class One licence and work for clients like Seypec, Lemuria Resort and the Ministry of Land Use and Habitat. Recently you won the tender for the Seychelles Pension Fund building. The website people find today was made in 2010, and it still shows the company as it was then.

What a client finds today

  • The newest project is from 2010. The work you've done since, including the Pension Fund building, isn't there yet.
  • It isn't built for phones. The whole desktop page shrinks onto the screen, so visitors have to pinch and zoom to read it.
  • Browsers label it "Not secure", because the site has no HTTPS. That's the first thing a tender panel or a villa client sees.
  • The footer still reads "Copyright © 2010".

People who look you up don't reach it

  • Your Google listing has no website. It shows "Add website", so anyone who searches for Mahé Design & Build gets a phone number and nothing to look at.
  • The contact details don't match. The site gives P.O. Box 601, Bel Eau, a six-digit phone number and a fax. Google lists East Coast Road, Victoria and 4 322 762.
  • The website doesn't link to your Facebook page, and there's no LinkedIn company page yet, so there's no single place where a client can see everything you build.
Why a website matters for a contractor

What a great site does for Mahé Design & Build

Before anyone calls a contractor, they look them up. A developer checking a shortlist, an architect choosing who to recommend, a villa owner abroad: they all want to see what you've built, and how well.

Tenders and shortlists

Look the part before the meeting

Evaluation panels, project managers and consultants check a contractor online. A current site with your licence, your projects and named clients backs up every bid.

Private clients

Villa owners often decide from abroad

Many people building a home in Seychelles live overseas for part of the year. Your projects, photos and a clear enquiry form let them get to know you from wherever they are.

Architects and consultants

A link they can pass on

Every project has its own page with the architect, engineer, year and scope. It's easy to send, and it shows the architects you've built for.

Better enquiries

Know what they want before you call back

The Start a project form asks what they're building, where, how far along they are and the budget, so your team can reply with the right person.

Credibility

Class One, since 2002, said up front

Your licence grade, your years in business, your clients and their own words about your work, all on the first screen a visitor scrolls through.

Found on Google

Your name leads somewhere

With a secure, phone-friendly site linked from your Google listing, searches for you and for "building contractor Seychelles" lead to your work instead of a blank listing.

The new site

A site plan that turns into a building as you scroll

Most contractor websites are a slideshow of finished buildings. This one shows how you build. The page is an architect's drawing sheet: as visitors scroll, the plan rises into a building, from the survey to handover, the way your projects do on site.

The full site is live for you to try. Open it on your phone, scroll the building up, look through the projects and try Start a project. It's on a private preview address and isn't listed on Google.

Survey & site plan

Drawn, then built

Every part of the building starts as fine graphite lines on the plan. As it rises it's hatched like a section drawing, then it turns into solid concrete, timber, glass and stone.

A short line beside each stage says what your team does at that point, in plain words.

A title block that's also the menu

In the corner sits a real drawing title block: project, sheet, scale and title. It updates as you scroll ("Sheet 05 of 06, Finishes"), and tapping a sheet number jumps straight to that stage.

The main menu is always at the top, on phones and computers.

Your projects, like a drawing register

All your projects in one list, with the year, the architect and the sector. Filter by resort, private villa, commercial, industrial or community. On a computer, a photo of each project appears as you move over it.

Recent work like the Pension Fund building can be added as soon as you have photos.

A page for every project

Each project has its own page: the client, the year, the architect, the engineer, the project manager where there was one, the scope of work, and the photos, which open full screen.

The photos in the concept are from your current site. New photos of recent projects would make these pages shine.

Credentials first

Your Class One licence, founded in 2002, design and build, turnkey or single stage. Below it are the clients you've built for, the architects you've worked with and your clients' own words about your work.

Start a project, in four questions

What are you building? Where is the site? Are you at the land, drawings, approvals or ready-to-build stage? And roughly what's the budget? A project brief fills in beside the form as they answer.

Then they send it to you by email or WhatsApp, with their name and number, so your team knows exactly who to call back.

The site is designed for phones first. Visitors who have turned off animations on their phone get the same content without the motion.

Questions

Things you might be wondering

Do we keep mahedesignbuild.com?

Yes. The new site goes live on the address you already own, with HTTPS, so old links and business cards still work.

How do we add new projects?

Send us the details and photos by email or WhatsApp and we'll add the project page. We'll talk through an aftercare option on the call, so updates are always quick.

We don't have photos of our recent work. Is that a problem?

Not at all. The site can launch with the projects you have photos of, and a project can show the drawing card until photos are ready. We can also photograph your projects for you.

Will the 3D scroll work on older phones?

Yes. It's built to run smoothly on everyday phones, and if a phone can't show 3D, the visitor gets a still drawing and all the same content.

Where do the projects, photos and testimonials come from?

All from your current website: the project list with years, architects and engineers, the photos, and your clients' testimonials, lightly shortened. We'd only put them live with your OK.

Where do enquiries go?

To your email and your WhatsApp, already filled in with what the client is building, where, their stage, their budget and how to reach them.

What if we want something different from the concept?

Tell us on the call. Small changes are free once you buy the site, and anything bigger is quoted before we start, so there are no surprises.
